problem_evidence.user_requirement: (1) The one stock the operator actually trades each day (surfaced by collect.py + predict.py) keeps being entered into the Google Sheet by hand -- that stays. (2) Everything else in the day's screened-but-untraded candidate pool must be handled entirely by project code from now on; the operator should not have to analyze it or type it into a spreadsheet. (3) Every field on those automated rows -- scenario and theme/sector included -- must come out correct, not blank/sentinel where a real value exists. (4) The current daily/ shape (collect.py -> archive.py -> Google Sheet round trip) is not sacred -- propose a better structure if one exists.
problem_evidence.collection_is_already_fully_automated: src/daily/collect.py:308-343 assigns 시나리오 through a deterministic rule cascade with zero human input: membership in upper_limit_stock_codes/upper_limit_next_day_stock_codes/new_high_stock_codes/near_new_high_stock_codes (populated from parallel KIS 조건검색 lookups), a close<open check for '상승형 음봉', an SMA120 breakout check, and a final fallback to '거래량 폭증'. collect.py:652-671 resolves 테마 through load_theme_from_db() + batch_resolve_missing_themes() with the code comment '테마 미매칭 종목 자동 분류 및 로컬 Parquet/DB 캐시 갱신 (구글 시트 수동 의존 제거)' -- theme resolution was already de-manualized before this session started.
problem_evidence.collect_csv_drops_the_theme_column_it_ju: save_collected_condition_data (src/daily/collect.py:80-110) does `out = out.reindex(columns=STANDARD_COLUMN_ORDER)` before writing settings.CONDITION_CSV_PATH, and STANDARD_COLUMN_ORDER (src/processing/schema.py:215-251) has no '테마'/'테마_섹터' entry -- so the theme collect.py just resolved and logged is silently dropped from the file archive.py reads next. This is harmless only because archive.py re-derives it independently (next finding); it is dead work, not a data-loss bug, since nothing downstream currently expects theme in the CSV.
problem_evidence.archive_py_independently_reconciles_scen: src/daily/archive.py:_standardize_archive_df (166-220) is the real source of archive.parquet's fields, run once at archive.py:main() (~472-509) when it ingests settings.CONDITION_CSV_PATH: theme is `out['테마_섹터'].fillna(out[STOCK_CODE_COL].map(load_theme())).fillna('테마 없음')` (same load_theme()/theme.parquet source this session's candidate_panel.py already reads via its theme_df parameter -- src/data/data_loader.py:53-62 confirms load_theme() prefers THEME_PARQUET_PATH); scenario is `out['시나리오']` if present else falls back through '차트분석' / 'Scenario_Base' / a final literal '기본 분석' sentinel, then strips legacy '_Y'/'_N' suffixes, then the raw '차트분석' column is dropped entirely from the archived row. Measured on data/history/archive.parquet: 시나리오 is 100% populated (거래량 폭증 362, 상따 49, 120 돌파 34, 신고가 25, 기본 분석 23, 상한가 다음날 10, 상승형 음봉 7, 신고가 근접 5) and 테마_섹터 is 100% populated (바이오 73, 반도체 59, 2차전지 51, 로봇 33, ...). Both are point-in-time values already resolved before the row is archived -- there is nothing left to reconstruct for archive.parquet-sourced rows.
problem_evidence.sheet_round_trip_has_no_candidate_push_a: src/data/gsheet_loader.py's only write path (append_stocks_to_gsheet, :176-232) targets the theme worksheet (코드_테마_DB), never Trade/Trade2 -- nothing in code pushes the day's candidate pool into the sheet for the operator to fill in. src/data/sync_sheet_db.py:sync_trade_log (:56 onward) pulls the ENTIRE Trade/Trade2 worksheets and does `df_trade.to_sql('table_trade_log', conn, if_exists='replace', ...)` with no 'is this the real trade' filter -- every row physically present in the sheet becomes a trade_log.parquet row. The historical 2016-2025 richness (69-84% of each day's candidate pool journaled, per the prior session's finding) came entirely from the operator manually pasting src/utils/export_archive.py / archive.render_tsv output into Trade/Trade2 and hand-filling hypothetical outcomes -- there is no code path that requires this. Stopping that manual paste habit (already done, per the operator) breaks nothing in the sheet-sync code.
problem_evidence.candidate_panel_theme_priority_is_backwa: src/data/candidate_panel.py::load_candidate_snapshot_panel (current session) computes `panel['(테마/섹터)'] = mapped.fillna(existing).fillna('기타')` where `mapped` comes from the caller-supplied theme_df and `existing` is the row's own already-resolved (테마/섹터) (real for archive rows, absent for condition_history rows). This lets a static theme_df snapshot silently overwrite an archive row's own point-in-time-resolved theme whenever theme_df also happens to have an entry for that code -- the opposite of the intended precedence. It is not caught by the existing test (test_load_candidate_snapshot_panel_uses_defaults_archive_and_theme, tests/unit/data/test_candidate_panel.py:198-243) because that test's theme_df has no entry for the archive-sourced symbol, so the bug never triggers there.
problem_evidence.no_theme_sentinel_is_split_across_two_sp: archive.py's own fallback writes the literal string '테마 없음' (src/daily/archive.py:188,190) while collect.py and candidate_panel.py's final fallback both use '기타' (src/daily/collect.py:667; src/data/candidate_panel.py). Left uncorrected, the reconstructed panel would carry two distinct 'no theme' categories that should be one, diluting an already-marginal categorical feature and confusing anything that groups by theme_sector.
problem_evidence.no_repeat_of_the_price_history_freeze_is: This session's own price_history.parquet freeze (fixed_end_date hardcoded to 2025-12-31 in src/backfill/price/config.py, silently stuck for ~8 months) was found only by manually running the restoration code and noticing 27 rows instead of thousands. Nothing today would surface a recurrence of that freeze, or of price_history simply not being refreshed on a given day, before it silently degrades candidate_panel.py's synthesis coverage back toward zero again.

objective: Turn the already-mostly-automated collect.py -> archive.py candidate pipeline plus this session's build_restored_trade_log into one recurring, inspectable daily step that needs no operator analysis or spreadsheet entry for the untraded remainder, fix the two correctness bugs found while tracing that pipeline (theme precedence, split no-theme sentinel), and add a staleness watchdog so the exact kind of silent freeze found this session cannot recur unnoticed. The Google Sheet keeps exactly its current, already-minimal job: the operator types in the one stock actually traded and its real fill prices. No change to collect.py's or archive.py's own scenario/theme resolution logic is needed -- it is already correct and already automated.

changes.name: load_candidate_snapshot_panel
changes.signature: def load_candidate_snapshot_panel(condition_history_path: Path | None = None, archive_df: pd.DataFrame | None = None, theme_df: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame
changes.detail: Fix theme precedence: normalize the literal '테마 없음' sentinel (and empty string) to NaN in the union's (테마/섹터) column BEFORE any fallback, then coalesce as `existing.fillna(mapped).fillna('기타')` -- an already-resolved value from condition_history/archive wins outright; theme_df (a static snapshot) fills in only where the source row itself has no theme; '기타' is the final catch-all. This is a precedence swap plus a sentinel-normalization step in the same block that currently reads `panel['(테마/섹터)'] = mapped.fillna(existing).fillna('기타')` -- do not change the '(차트분석)' handling, which already correctly leaves archive rows untouched and only sentinels condition_history rows.

changes.name: ARCHIVE_SCENARIO_THEME_AUTHENTIC_SINCE
changes.detail: Literal '2026-08-04' (archive.py's own operational start date, per docs/decisions/task_index.json TASK_ARCHIVE_SNAPSHOT_DEDUP_ON_RERUN and this session's measurement of archive.parquet's date range). Purely documentary/assertable -- used by the new regression test to state in one place why archive-sourced rows never receive UNSCORED_SCENARIO_SENTINEL, instead of that invariant being implicit in the branch structure alone.

changes.name: NO_THEME_SENTINELS
changes.detail: frozenset({'테마 없음', ''}) -- the set of upstream 'no theme resolved' spellings that load_candidate_snapshot_panel normalizes to NaN before the theme fallback chain, so they never survive as a value distinct from the panel's own '기타' catch-all.

changes.name: check_price_history_freshness
changes.signature: def check_price_history_freshness(price_history_df: pd.DataFrame, *, as_of: pd.Timestamp | None = None, max_staleness_days: int = 5) -> dict[str, Any]
changes.detail: Compute `staleness_days = (as_of or pd.Timestamp.today().normalize()) - price_history_df['date'].max()` (calendar days; a 5-day default absorbs weekends plus one holiday without false-positive noise) and return {'max_date': <str>, 'staleness_days': <int>, 'is_stale': staleness_days > max_staleness_days}. Pure function, no logging or raising -- callers decide what to do with the verdict. This is the reusable primitive behind the new daily script's watchdog log line; it must not itself block anything, since a stale price_history should degrade synthesis coverage gracefully (as it already does, per attach_reconstructed_labels' next-open availability check) rather than crash the daily run.

changes.name: main
changes.signature: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None
changes.detail: New daily CLI, same shape as src/daily/archive.py's main(): parse --trade-log/--theme/--price-history/--condition-history/--out (defaults to settings.TRADE_LOG_PARQUET_PATH, settings.THEME_PARQUET_PATH, settings.PRICE_HISTORY_PARQUET_PATH, settings.HISTORY_DIR/'condition_history_cleaned.parquet', and settings.PARQUET_DIR/'ml_training_panel.parquet' respectively). Loads those inputs, calls check_price_history_freshness and logs a WARNING '[DATA] stage=ml_panel_freshness status=stale max_date=... staleness_days=... threshold_days=...' when stale (still proceeds -- staleness degrades coverage, it does not invalidate what synthesis is possible), calls build_restored_trade_log, writes the result to --out via write_price_history_parquet's codec conventions (zstd, float32 downcast for the numeric panel columns -- reuse src.data.parquet_codec, do not hand-roll a second codec), and logs one INFO summary line '[DATA] stage=ml_panel_materialize rows=... restored_rows=... restored_dates=... execution_offset_pct=... out=...' from the result's .attrs['panel_restoration']. Also logs a non-blocking INFO health signal '[DATA] stage=ml_panel_daily_volume date=... rows=... status=...' for the most recent EXECUTED_LABEL_SOURCE trade_date, where status is 'nominal' when that day's executed-row count is <= 3 and 'elevated' otherwise -- a lightweight nudge (never a gate) in case the operator drifts back into pasting bulk candidates into the sheet without meaning to. Idempotent: rerunning with unchanged inputs overwrites --out with byte-for-byte-equivalent content (same guarantee build_restored_trade_log's own sort-then-reset already provides).

changes.name: main
changes.signature: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None
changes.detail: In the existing `elif not args.no_restore_panel:` branch (right before or after calling build_restored_trade_log), call check_price_history_freshness(price_history_df) and log a WARNING '[DATA] stage=ml_panel_freshness status=stale max_date=... staleness_days=... threshold_days=...' when the result's is_stale is True -- same log shape as the new daily script, so the exact failure mode found this session (retrain.py silently training on a frozen price_history) is now visible in retrain.py's own log output, not only in a separate script the operator might forget to run. Non-blocking per R6: retrain.py proceeds exactly as it does today regardless of the verdict.

requirements: R1 (sheet contract unchanged): no change to sync_sheet_db.py, gsheet_loader.py, or the Trade/Trade2 worksheet schema. The operator's daily manual step stays exactly what it is today -- type in the one real trade.

R2 (no re-derivation of already-correct fields): do not add any code that re-derives or second-guesses collect.py's scenario cascade or archive.py's theme/scenario reconciliation for rows that already carry a real value. The only new logic is precedence/normalization at the point candidate_panel.py merges sources, per the theme-priority fix above.

R3 (archive authenticity is absolute): a row sourced from archive.parquet must never receive UNSCORED_SCENARIO_SENTINEL or an overwritten theme, regardless of what theme_df contains for that code. Only condition_history_cleaned.parquet-sourced rows (the pre-archive.py window) may carry the scenario sentinel, and even those keep their own real theme when they have one.

R4 (no-theme sentinel unification): '테마 없음' and '' are treated as missing, never as a fourth theme category alongside a code's real theme, theme_df's mapped value, and the '기타' catch-all -- there must be exactly one no-theme spelling ('기타') in candidate_panel.py's output.

R5 (materialized artifact is additive, not authoritative): src/daily/materialize_ml_panel.py writes a NEW file (ml_training_panel.parquet); it must never write to settings.TRADE_LOG_PARQUET_PATH or otherwise mutate the operator's sheet-synced ground truth. src/ml/retrain.py is NOT changed to depend on this artifact -- it keeps calling build_restored_trade_log inline (already correct, already tested, ~4.5s on the full corpus) so a skipped or stale materialization run can never cause retrain.py to silently train on outdated data.

R6 (freshness watchdog is observability, not a gate): check_price_history_freshness and its WARNING log must never raise or block main() from completing -- a stale price_history should still materialize whatever it can (which may be zero new rows, as already happens gracefully) rather than fail the daily run.

R7 (idempotency): rerunning src/daily/materialize_ml_panel.py with unchanged inputs and the same --out path overwrites it with row-for-row identical content; it never appends or accumulates duplicates across runs.

R8 (dtype/storage discipline): the materialized parquet follows the same zstd + float32-downcast convention as the rest of the price/candidate corpus (src/data/parquet_codec.py) -- no new ad-hoc snappy/float64 artifact.

R9 (volume nudge is informational only): the '일별 실행 행수' health-check log line must never raise, block, or filter rows -- it is a visibility aid, not a validation gate, since the operator may legitimately paste more than one hypothetical row on a given day and that must keep working.

R10 (retrain.py surfaces the same watchdog): src/ml/retrain.py logs the identical stale/fresh verdict via check_price_history_freshness whenever it runs the restoration path, so staleness is visible at the point of training even if the operator never runs src/daily/materialize_ml_panel.py that day. This must not change retrain.py's control flow or gate anything -- log only.

design_rationale.alternatives_considered: (a) Push collect.py's daily candidate list directly into the Google Sheet (Trade/Trade2 or a new tab) so the operator has something to look at -- rejected: the operator's stated goal is to see LESS spreadsheet surface, not a new auto-populated tab to scroll past; predict.py already prints the ranked candidate table to the terminal for the operator to decide what to trade, which is the only place a human decision needs to happen. (b) Rebuild scenario/theme in candidate_panel.py from raw OHLCV/condition-search membership, mirroring collect.py's own cascade -- rejected: collect.py and archive.py already do this correctly and it is already in the data (measured: 100% populated on both fields in archive.parquet); re-deriving it a second time downstream would risk disagreeing with the value collect.py actually decided on for that historical moment, for zero benefit. (c) Make src/ml/retrain.py read the new materialized parquet instead of calling build_restored_trade_log inline -- rejected: this makes retrain.py's correctness depend on a separate daily job having run recently, reintroducing exactly the 'silent staleness nobody notices' failure mode this whole spec exists to close off elsewhere; the inline call is cheap enough (4.5s) that there is no performance reason to avoid it. (d) Retire/delete src/utils/export_archive.py and archive.render_tsv since the bulk-paste habit they supported is no longer needed -- rejected: they cost nothing to keep, remain useful as an ad-hoc manual audit view if the operator ever wants to eyeball a day's candidates, and deleting a working utility on the strength of a workflow-habit change is unrelated scope. (e) Enforce the 'sheet should only ever contain one row per day' rule with a hard validation error -- rejected per R9: it is a legitimate choice for the operator to log more than the one real trade on some days (e.g. resuming manual journaling for a specific research question), and a hard gate would fight that instead of just surfacing it.
design_rationale.chosen_reason: Tracing the actual pipeline (this spec's context_files) shows the user's stated goal -- stop analyzing and typing the untraded remainder into a spreadsheet -- is already structurally achieved by collect.py + archive.py + this session's candidate_panel.py; there is no missing automation to build for scenario/theme, only two precedence/consistency bugs in how candidate_panel.py merges already-correct sources, plus the operational gap that the restoration only ever runs implicitly, in-memory, inside retrain.py. Making it a standalone, scheduled-by-the-operator daily script with its own log line turns 'is the untraded remainder being captured correctly today' from an invisible property of the ML training code into something checkable in under a second by reading one log line -- which is the actual leverage point, since the freeze this session found (§ price_history_freeze) went undetected for ~8 months precisely because nothing surfaced it.
failure_modes: Theme precedence fix applied to the wrong direction (still letting theme_df win) would silently reintroduce inconsistency between a row's archived theme and its reconstructed-panel theme for the same (date, code) whenever the operator later re-exports theme.parquet. Guard: R3/R4 plus an explicit regression test asserting the archive-sourced theme survives a conflicting theme_df entry.

Sentinel unification miscounts '기타' as an already-real theme and drops it during normalization, turning legitimately-unresolved rows into NaN and breaking the categorical fillna contract build_ml_dataset expects (_CATEGORICAL_COLUMNS fillna('Unknown')). Guard: NO_THEME_SENTINELS is scoped to exactly {'테마 없음', ''} and must never include '기타' itself.

The new daily script silently overwrites ml_training_panel.parquet with an EMPTIER result than yesterday's (e.g. transient price_history read failure) and nothing notices. Guard: R6's freshness log plus the INFO summary line always reporting restored_rows -- an operator or a future monitoring script can diff that number day over day without new code.

The freshness watchdog is added only to the new standalone script and never reaches the training pipeline itself, so the one place this session's actual bug occurred (retrain.py silently degrading to near-zero synthesis) stays just as silent as before. Guard: R10 wires check_price_history_freshness into retrain.py's own restoration branch too, not only into materialize_ml_panel.py.

performance_budget.expected_data_scale: Same inputs as build_restored_trade_log (trade_log ~34-40k rows, price_history ~5.5M rows column-pruned to date/symbol/open/close, condition_history ~5-6k rows, archive growing by ~15-20 rows/day). check_price_history_freshness is a single max() over an already-loaded column -- O(1) relative to the existing 4.5s restoration cost it wraps.
performance_budget.storage_format: parquet, zstd, via src/data/parquet_codec.py -- reuse the existing codec helpers rather than a new one
performance_budget.dtype_precision: float32 for the materialized panel's OHLCV/flow columns (matching _PANEL_FLOAT32_COLUMNS in candidate_panel.py); float64 preserved only for the label arithmetic already inside build_restored_trade_log
performance_budget.chunking_strategy: no chunking needed -- the full restored panel is a single in-memory frame well under the memory budget; write it in one parquet call

def test_load_candidate_snapshot_panel_prefers_archived_theme_over_theme_df(tmp_path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    import pandas as pd

    from src import settings
    from src.daily import archive
    from src.data import candidate_panel as mod

    # Arrange: no condition_history, one archive row already resolved to '반도체'.
    history_dir = tmp_path / "history"
    history_dir.mkdir()
    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "HISTORY_DIR", history_dir)
    arch = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "스냅샷_날짜": ["2026-08-10"],
            "종목코드": ["005930"],
            "종가": [100.0],
            "거래대금": [500.0],
            "등락률": [1.0],
            "시장구분": ["KOSPI"],
            "시나리오": ["신고가"],
            "테마_섹터": ["반도체"],
        }
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(archive, "fetch_archive_snapshot", lambda all_rows=False, **kw: arch)
    # A conflicting, stale theme_df entry for the same code.
    theme_df = pd.DataFrame({"종목코드": ["005930"], "테마": ["2차전지"]})

    # Act
    panel = mod.load_candidate_snapshot_panel(theme_df=theme_df)

    # Assert: the archive-resolved theme wins, not theme_df's conflicting entry.
    assert panel.loc[0, "(테마/섹터)"] == "반도체"
    assert panel.loc[0, "(차트분석)"] == "신고가"

def test_check_price_history_freshness_flags_stale_data() -> None:
    import pandas as pd

    from src.data.candidate_panel import check_price_history_freshness

    # Arrange
    stale = pd.DataFrame({"date": pd.to_datetime(["2025-12-30"])})
    fresh = pd.DataFrame({"date": pd.to_datetime(["2026-09-03", "2026-09-04"])})
    as_of = pd.Timestamp("2026-09-05")

    # Act
    stale_result = check_price_history_freshness(stale, as_of=as_of, max_staleness_days=5)
    fresh_result = check_price_history_freshness(fresh, as_of=as_of, max_staleness_days=5)

    # Assert
    assert stale_result["is_stale"] is True
    assert stale_result["staleness_days"] == (as_of - pd.Timestamp("2025-12-30")).days
    assert fresh_result["is_stale"] is False
    assert fresh_result["staleness_days"] == 1
